clue.text: Business to get involved in by force

parts.note: to enter into something is to become involved in it
to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: A firm muscling its way into a deal by strong-arm methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial venture or company is called an enterprise, a synonym for a business.

clue.text: Look up about fifty elusive people

indicators.note: about tells us the turned word goes around the Roman numeral
in a down clue, up tells us to read the word for look from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to look is to see
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone searching for some fifty people who keep slipping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEE into EES, and 'about' puts L inside it. The definition plays on the phrase 'slippery as an eel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery types are idiomatically called eels, since the fish is notoriously hard to grasp.

clue.text: The outside broadcast is his forte

definitions.text: The outside broadcast is his forte

parts.words: The outside broadcast is his forte
parts.note: an outside broadcast sounds like television, but it is a man whose speciality is shouting news aloud in the open street

explanation.definitionFit: A town's official announcer once proclaimed public notices in the streets, a literal outdoor broadcast.

clue.text: Equestrian appendage

explanation.definitionFit: A horseman is one sense; the other is an added clause attached to a document or verdict.

clue.text: Corded stuff isn't commonly put on a new coat

parts.note: rep is a fabric with a corded, ribbed surface
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Ribbed fabric that is not usually used to make a fresh coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests clothing, matching the fabric in the surface, but it is a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying another layer of paint is what it means to give something a fresh coat.

clue.text: Good person, ready for a change, sinned

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a crossword staple for a good person

indicators.note: the letters of ready are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A virtuous person, eager for something different, went astray morally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' turns READY into RAYED, placed after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray from the right path is a common metaphor for doing wrong morally.

clue.text: Fine powder available in metal canisters

indicators.note: the answer is available inside the run of letters of metal canisters

explanation.surface: A soft powder sold in tins.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral is ground into a soft dusting powder used on skin.

clue.text: Correct guys in publicity

indicators.note: in tells us the word for guys sits inside the word for publicity

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
guys means men

explanation.surface: Fix the men pictured in an advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right or revise something is to correct it.

clue.text: Net account for providing church lighting

parts.note: a net profit is a clear profit, after deductions
a story is an account of events

explanation.surface: A profit-and-loss statement that pays for a church's lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of clerestory, the upper row of windows that lights a church nave.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper windowed wall of a nave lets daylight into the building.

clue.text: Concerned with track access

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a course is a track, as for racing

explanation.surface: Someone worried about getting onto a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Having resort to something, such as legal remedy, is having access to it.

clue.text: With the sovereign due, created a beastly row

parts.note: a sovereign is a one-pound coin, and L stands for pound
money due is money owed

explanation.surface: A loud protest about a gold coin still to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin worth one pound; L (from Latin libra) is the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle mooing make a noise from animals, a literal beastly row.

clue.text: French family-man accepting break to keep going

indicators.note: accepting means the French father takes the word for break inside him

parts.note: pere is French for father
to sever is to break

explanation.surface: A French father taking a holiday so he can carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: Persisting despite difficulty is carrying on, continuing.

clue.text: Mark urban area's poverty

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: The blight of deprivation in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortage or dearth is a sense of poverty, as in a poverty of ideas.

clue.text: Instruct a class

explanation.definitionFit: To command is one sense; the other is a taxonomic or social rank or group.

clue.text: Keep access!

parts.note: keep sounds like a command to retain entry, but a keep is a castle tower and this is the lifting way across the moat into it

explanation.definitionFit: The raisable span over a moat gives entry to a castle and its stronghold tower.

clue.text: Dress hire cut by intention

indicators.note: cut by means the word for intention splits the word for hire

parts.note: to rent is to hire
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: A gown rental reduced on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or garments in archaic, literary language is attire.

clue.text: Going in for charm

explanation.definitionFit: A way in or the act of coming in is one sense; as a verb, to enchant or delight is the other.

clue.text: Hibernating insects without number

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the insects go around the number

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle, an insect
the ant is the second insect
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: Bugs asleep for winter, with nothing to count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: DOR and ANT surround M. DOR is a dung beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal sleeping through winter is inactive and inert, lying quiet.

clue.text: Ancient scientist claims the compound made

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: An old chemist asserts that his mixture has been produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemist's noun, but it signals the anagram; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval practitioner sought to turn base metals into gold, a forerunner of the chemist.

clue.text: Beaten, and that's material

explanation.definitionFit: To be bested or defeated is one sense; the other is a smooth woollen yarn or cloth.

clue.text: The doctor includes everyone that's idler

indicators.note: includes means the doctor's abbreviation holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: all means everyone
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: The GP takes on all comers, so who is the lazy one?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dawdles or wastes time is a loafer.

clue.text: An artist's jacket

explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Spencer was an English painter; the word also names a short close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Plain van, as an organisation required

indicators.note: the letters need organising, that is rearranging into a new order

explanation.surface: A plain-looking van, as a company needs one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as a description of the van, but it is the definition: a grassy plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical grassland with scattered trees is an open, flat expanse of land.

clue.text: The odd scholar makes music

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
BA, Bachelor of Arts, a graduate or scholar

explanation.surface: An eccentric academic plays a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban dance rhythm is a style of Latin American dance tune.

clue.text: A Scotsman carrying gold-the fool!

indicators.note: carrying means the Scots word holds the heraldic gold inside

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A Scot laden with gold is mocked as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot or stupid person is a fool, synonyms in insult.

clue.text: Spent recklessly — laid on about six

indicators.note: about tells us the word for laid on goes around the Roman six

parts.note: to lay on is to strike, to lash
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone splurged and treated half a dozen friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending or giving extravagantly is to bestow freely without restraint.

clue.text: Payment commonly secured by a twister

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wage or salary is the first sense; a threaded fastener turned into place is the second.

clue.text: Old ruler seen in his finest sarong

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the run of letters of finest sarong

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch dressed up in his best wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor of Russia before 1917 bore this title.

clue.text: Track supervision

explanation.definitionFit: A route or course is one sense; guidance and management, as of a film, is the other.

clue.text: City miser's rehoused

indicators.note: rehoused means the letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A town where a skinflint has been moved to new lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: A high-flier has merit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer is a word pronounced the same as the word for merit

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A successful achiever deserves credit, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a successful person, but it is a sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle soars at height, so it is literally a bird that flies high.

clue.text: The sea mole

parts.note: mole suggests a burrowing animal, but here it is a stone pier built out into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive harbour wall that shelters ships from waves.
